title: GRACE and GRACE-FO JPL Mascon Terrestrial Water Storage Anomalies (RL06.3Mv04, CRI)
description: Monthly anomalies of total terrestrial water storage (equivalent water thickness, cm, relative to a time mean) derived from the GRACE (2002–2017) and GRACE-FO (2018– ) satellite gravimetry missions and processed at NASA JPL with the mascon approach: 4,551 equal-area 3° spherical-cap mass concentrations, provided on a 0.5° grid, with a Coastal Resolution Improvement filter, uncertainties, land mask and optional gain (scale) factors.
purpose: The only global observation of total water-storage change (groundwater + soil moisture + surface water), relevant to monitoring long-term storage trends in Algeria's large aquifer systems and to drought impacts at basin scale.

spatial_extent.description: Global (CMR bounding rectangle −180/−90/180/90) on a 0.5° grid; the underlying resolution is set by the 3° equal-area mascons (about 300 km), so Algeria (about 2.4 million km2) is represented by roughly two dozen independent mascons (AEO estimate from area, not a provider statement). Users subset the single global file.

temporal_extent.description: April 2002 to present; the single file available on 2026-11-21 (GRCTellus.JPL.200204_202609.GLO.RL06.3M.MSCNv04CRI) runs to September 2026. The record has missing months, including the gap between the GRACE and GRACE-FO missions.

resolution.spatial: 0.5° grid; effective resolution of 3° equal-area mascons

variables.name: lwe_thickness
variables.description: Liquid water equivalent thickness anomaly relative to the time mean

variables.name: scale_factor (gain factors)
variables.description: Optional gain factors for land hydrology, provided with the solution

variables.name: land_mask / mascon_ID
variables.description: Land mask used by the CRI filter and mascon identifiers

processing: Monthly gravity-field variations are solved directly on geolocated spherical-cap mascons using K-band range-rate and GPS data, with geophysical a-priori constraints that remove correlated errors, so no de-striping or smoothing is needed. GIA is modelled with ICE-6G_D, the C20 coefficient is replaced following TN-14 and the geocenter follows TN-13 processing standards (release notes). RL06.3Mv04 uses the ACX2 accelerometer-transplant bundle for GRACE-FO months in wide dead-band pointing; the 21 October 2026 release fixed two minor bugs from the August 2026 solution onward.
validation: Uncertainties are provided per mascon and were recalibrated for the GRACE-FO period in v4.0 (release notes). No single accuracy figure is given on the catalogue page; Watkins et al. (2015) and Wiese et al. (2016) describe the method and leakage-error assessment.
limitations: Measures total water storage change only; separating groundwater requires subtracting soil moisture, snow and surface-water storage from models or other observations, which adds large uncertainty.

Effective resolution of about 300 km: individual Algerian basins, dams or irrigated perimeters cannot be resolved; signals near the Mediterranean coast are affected by land–ocean leakage despite the CRI filter.
Anomalies are relative to a time mean; absolute storage is not provided.
Missing months and the 2017–2018 inter-mission gap must be handled in trend analysis; processing updates (e.g. v4.0 in 2024, bug fixes in 2025 and 2026) slightly change earlier values.
Downloads require a free NASA Earthdata Login.

algeria_notes: Relevant for regional storage trends over the North-Western Sahara Aquifer System shared with Tunisia and Libya and over the Tell basins, but only at a scale of several hundred kilometres. Interpret Saharan signals together with irrigation and abstraction information, and treat any groundwater estimate derived from GRACE as a model-dependent residual, not a measurement.
